summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DNS resolver for the shared lan network (10.50.50.0/24), answering authoritatively for inventory.internal with node2's lan address and forwarding all other queries to public upstreams; configured node2 and node3 to resolve through node1. Implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4), targeting node1 via raw VyOS configure-mode commands and node2/node3 via nmcli (through ansible.builtin.raw, since RHEL7's python2 was incompatible with modern ansible-core modules). Verified functionally, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on all 4 nodes.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS (dual-homed mgmt+lan), node2/node3=RHEL7.9 (dual-homed mgmt+lan), node4=Ubuntu 24.04 ansible-controller (mgmt only), lan network 10.100.222.0/24-independent private /24 with dhcp=false requiring manual addressing

Authorized the cluster SSH keypair for node4->node1 (via VyOS 'system login user vyos authentication public-keys') and node4->node2/node3 (appended CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to antrieb user's authorized_keys)

Ansible play 1 (host node1/vyos): raw bash -c VyOS configure block setting eth1 address 10.50.50.10/24, system static-host-mapping inventory.internal -> 10.50.50.11, service dns forwarding listen-address 10.50.50.10, allow-from 10.50.50.0/24, upstream name-servers 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9; commit+save

Ansible play 2 (hosts node2/node3, become sudo): raw nmcli commands assigning static lan IPs (10.50.50.11/.12), setting ipv4.dns 10.50.50.10 with ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes on eth1, and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes on eth0 so node1 is the sole resolver
Ran ansible-playbook from node4 against inventory.ini; confirmed idempotent success on rerun
Verified pdns_recursor listening on node1's lan IP:53, and getent hosts on node2/node3 resolving inventory.internal to node2's address and example.com via upstream forwarding

Captured boot_id + service/data health baseline on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot, polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified DNS resolution/config persistence after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DNS resolver answering inventory.internal with node2's lan address and forwarding everything else upstream
evidence.summary: VyOS commit applied static-host-mapping (inventory.internal->10.50.50.11) and dns forwarding (listen 10.50.50.10, allow-from 10.50.50.0/24, upstream 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9); pdns_recursor confirmed listening on 10.50.50.10:53

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run set eth1 static IPs (10.50.50.11/.12) with DNS=10.50.50.10 and disabled eth0 auto-DNS; getent hosts on both nodes resolves inventory.internal to 10.50.50.11 and forwards example.com externally

evidence.requirement: Implementation performed via Ansible from the designated control_node
evidence.summary: inventory.ini and dns_playbook.yml created and executed via ansible-playbook on node4, the environment's configured control_node
